original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

actual_scope: On the two fixed local words of the highest open claims (#1324 and #1305, both on #1297's words, owners and dispatch), do the #1274/#1297 two-shock helper-donor kernels (both restoration rules) or exact re-timings of early reads improve the exactly optimal frames for any of the 306 helper pivots read before their first write; and is #1305's idle selection optimal within its admitted donor-star class?
scope_change_reason: The card asks about the selected packing; the selected #1094 is superseded by open claims on the same lineage, and #1288 already reports packing/width-neutral saturation on the #1218 words. The open question that matters for the highest claim is #1297's own next question: whether the helper-donor kernel family extends beyond its four analogous pivots on the final words, plus whether #1305's idle selection leaves headroom in its class.
bottleneck_link: The complex supplier binds; every recent gain on this line came from width-neutral local word changes (kernels) or idle repartitions. This bounds both families on the incumbent words and maps where a richer compensation would have to act.
stop_rule: Stop after exhaustive two-shock (both restoration rules) and re-timing censuses on both words with exact pricing; build an admitted construction only if a gain appears; one bounded pivot only.
evidence: evidence/CENSUS-*, PRICES-* (0 gains in 2 x (61 + 292) exact relation candidates), RETIME-* (0 gains in 2 x 803 exact moves), DELETION-* (screen only; control shows it is not a bound), IDLE-OPTIMUM-1305.json (#1305 selection = exact group optimum in all 3,687 groups); RESULT.json tallies; verify.py replays the censuses exactly and runs one positive and four failure controls. #1324 (posted during the census) uses the same word blobs; verdicts are unchanged at its endpoint weights, and it supersedes the idle part with a larger swap class.
author: Marius-Paul Dumitrean
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance from Anthropic Claude (Claude Code): search design, code, runs, analysis and text.

open_questions.question: Do three-shock or window-donor relations exist for the high-screen pivots (438/440 and the ten -51,648 pivots 226/228/230/231/232/236/238/434/436/446)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Their uncompensated deletion prices are 4-5x a realized #1274-type kernel (about +1.2e-6 kappa each if fully realized), and the two-shock family is now exhausted on these words.
open_questions.first_step: Extend census.py from output-read donor pairs to windows x += c*q ... x -= c*q on any register x closing before the first write of q; solve d as a sparse dyadic combination of at most three terms; price with price.py.
open_questions.blocked_by: About 2,500 distinct suffix vectors per pivot; all-triples enumeration is too large without support-guided pruning.
